'''Awawa Shrine''' (あわわじんじゃ, ''Awawa Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Hatsuma, {{ill|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|ar|كاكيغاوا (شيزوكا)|azb|کاکهقاوا، شیزوئوکا|ce|Какегава|ceb|Kakegawa|cs|Kakegawa (Šizuoka)|de|Kakegawa|eo|Kakegaŭa|es|Kakegawa|et|Kakegawa|fa|کاکه‌گاوا، شیزوئوکا|fi|Kakegawa|fr|Kakegawa|gl|Kakegawa|id|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|it|Kakegawa|ja|掛川市|ko|가케가와시|mg|Kakegawa|mzn|کاکه‌گاوا، شیزوئوکا|nl|Kakegawa|no|Kakegawa|pl|Kakegawa|pt|Kakegawa|ro|Kakegawa|ru|Какегава|sh|Kakegava|simple|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|sr|Какегава|sv|Kakegawa|tg|Какегава|th|คาเกงาวะ|tl|Kakegawa|tr|Kakegawa|tt|Какегава|uk|Какеґава (Сідзуока)|ur|کاکیگاوا|vi|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|war|Kakegawa, Shizuoka|zh|掛川市|zh_classical|掛川市|zh_min_nan|Kakegawa-chhī|zh_yue|掛川|qid=Q823988}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is enshrined near the summit of {{ill|Awa-ga-take|ceb|Awaga Dake (bukid sa Hapon, Shizuoka-ken)|ja|粟ヶ岳 (静岡県)|lld|Awa-ga-take|qid=Q11604550|lt=Mount Awagatake}}.

=== Overview ===
[[Image:Awagatake04.jpg|thumb|200px|View of the surrounding area from the summit of [[Mount Awagatake (Shizuoka Prefecture)|Mount Awagatake]]]]
The shrine enshrines Awahime-no-Mikoto as its {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100}} and was founded in {{ill|736|ab|736|af|736|am|736 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|736|ar|736|ary|736|ast|736|az|736|azb|۷۳۶ (میلادی)|bar|736|be|736|be_x_old|736|bg|736|bn|৭৩৬|bpy|মারি ৭৩৬|br|736|bs|736.|ca|736|cdo|736 nièng|ceb|736|ckb|٧٣٦|crh|736|cs|736|cv|736|cy|736|da|736|de|736|el|736|eml|736|eo|736|es|736|et|736|eu|736|fa|۷۳۶ (میلادی)|fi|736|fo|736|fr|736|fy|736|ga|736|gan|736年|gd|736|gl|736|he|736|hi|736|hr|736.|ht|736 (almanak jilyen)|hu|736|hy|736|id|736|io|736|is|736|it|736|ja|736年|jv|736|ka|736|kaa|736|kk|736 жыл|ko|736년|la|736|lb|736|lij|736|lmo|736|lt|736 m.|map_bms|736|mdf|736|mg|736|mhr|736|mk|736|mr|इ.स. ७३६|mrj|736 и|ms|736|mzn|۷۳۶|nah|736|nap|736|nds|736|new|सन् ७३६|nl|736|nn|736|no|736|nrm|736|nso|736|oc|736|or|୭୩୬|os|736-æм аз|pl|736|pnb|736|pt|736|qu|736|ro|736|ru|736 год|rue|736|sa|७३६|scn|736|sd|736ع|sh|736.|shn|736|si|736|sk|736|sl|736|sq|736|sr|736|su|736|sv|736|sw|736|tg|Соли 736|th|พ.ศ. 1279|tk|736|tl|736|tly|736|tr|736|tt|736 ел|uk|736|ur|736ء|uz|736|vec|736|vi|736|war|736|wuu|736年|xmf|736|zh|736年|zh_min_nan|736 nî|zh_yue|736年|qid=Q23581}}<ref name=yuisho>“[https://web.archive.org/web/20090615071355/http://www10.plala.or.jp/awawajinjya/sub1.html#Anchor-14490 History]” Awawa Shrine.</ref>. Within the {{ill|keidai|ja|境内|qid=Q11429002}} of Awawa Shrine, there is also {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|ar|معبد يايغاكي|fr|Yaegaki-jinja|ja|八重垣神社|qid=Q3571285}}, which enshrines {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Kushinadahime|lt=Kushinadahime|Q505469|qid=Q505469|lt=Kushinada-hime}}<ref name=yuisho/>.

The surrounding area is covered with {{ill|Laurel forest|Q788099|qid=Q788099}}. This forest has been designated by Kakegawa City as a {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|fa|املاک فرهنگی (ژاپن)|fr|Patrimoine culturel du Japon|id|Properti Kebudayaan (Jepang)|ja|文化財|tr|Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|zh|日本文化财|qid=Q858308}} under the name “Shrine Grove of Awawa Shrine” and is protected as a {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}}<ref>“[https://web.archive.org/web/20090615065637/http://www10.plala.or.jp/awawajinjya/sub9saiji.html Seasonal Festival and Prayer Information at Awawa Shrine]” Awawa Shrine.</ref><ref name=sitennenkinenbutu>Kakegawa City Board of Education, Lifelong Learning Division, Cultural Promotion Office, Cultural Properties Section, “[https://web.archive.org/web/20071208174729/http://lgportal.city.kakegawa.shizuoka.jp/kanko/bunkazai/sisiteibunkazai/sitennenkinenbutu.jsp City-designated Natural Monuments]”, Kakegawa City Hall, {{ill|April 1|Q2510|qid=Q2510}}.</ref>. Large rocks can be found scattered throughout this {{ill|Forest|Q4421|qid=Q4421|lt=forest}}, and these were worshipped as {{ill|Iwakura rock|Q11587880|qid=Q11587880}} (sacred rocks)<ref name=yuisho/><ref name=sitennenkinenbutu/>.

=== History ===
Since its founding in 736, the shrine was listed as an {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Engishiki shrine|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and attracted great reverence, receiving the protection of the {{ill|Castellan|Q1505781|qid=Q1505781}} of {{ill|Kakegawa Castle|Q2969457|qid=Q2969457}}<ref name=yuisho/>. However, after the shrine buildings were destroyed by fire during the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023}}, maintenance of the shrine stagnated until the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}<ref name=yuisho/>. In the Meiji period, the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and restoration progressed, including the reconstruction of the {{ill|Honden|Q2044994|qid=Q2044994}} and {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}} in {{ill|1884|Q7819|qid=Q7819}}<ref name=yuisho/>. After another period of stagnation due to the {{ill|Pacific War|Q184425|qid=Q184425}}, further development was carried out, including the relocation of the main hall to the mountaintop in {{ill|1987|Q2429|qid=Q2429}}<ref name=yuisho/>.

=== The Bell of Mugen on Mount Awagatake ===
This bell is counted as one of the {{ill|Seven Mysteries of Enshū|Q11642075|qid=Q11642075}}. It was a {{ill|Bonshō|Q8192099|qid=Q8192099}} formerly located at Mugen-yama Kannon-ji, a neighboring temple. It was said that those who struck the bell would fall into {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Avīci Hell}} after death, but would gain immense wealth in this life. It is said that around the {{ill|Meiō|cs|Meió|fa|میئو|ff|Meiō|fr|Ère Meiō|it|Meiō|ja|明応|ko|메이오|ru|Мэйо (нэнго)|simple|Meiō|sr|Меио|sv|Meiō|tr|Meiō|zh|明應 (日本)|qid=Q1193841}}, a concerned {{ill|Abbot (Buddhism)|Q1135621|qid=Q1135621}} sank the bell into a {{ill|Well|Q43483|qid=Q43483}}. This well remains within the precincts of Awawa Shrine<ref name=yuisho/><ref name="kokkai">“[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1347621/1/101 Tōkai Literature Walking Tour: Suruga and Tōtōmi Edition]” National Diet Library Digital Collection.</ref>.

In later times, it came to be believed that throwing a broken branch of sakaki upside down into this well would confer the same merit as striking the bell<ref name="kokkai"/>.

Kannon-ji was merged into Jōgen-ji Temple in Kakegawa City in {{ill|1961|Q3696|qid=Q3696}} and subsequently abolished<ref>“[http://33kannon.com/temple-no27/%E6%B0%97%E3%81%BE%E3%81%90%E3%82%8C%E3%81%AA%E5%B7%A1%E7%A4%BC%E6%A1%88%E5%86%85%E3%89%91/ Capricious Pilgrimage Guide (21)]” Tōtōmi Thirty-three Kannon Sacred Sites.</ref>.
